{"candidate_slot":0,"current_prompt":"You are given JSON input with two fields: 'system_profile' (a description or listing of installed hardware, OS, packages, libraries, and their versions) and 'advisories' (a supplied list of CVE entries, each with an ID, description, and 'affected' information such as product names and version ranges). Determine which of the SUPPLIED advisories apply to this installed system and return only their IDs.

Procedure:

1. Build the inventory: Extract every product, package, component, library, dependency, submodule, firmware, and OS name mentioned in system_profile, together with any version, edition, build, architecture, or vendor information. Record each item exactly as stated, including version strings that appear in package names, file paths, library versions, and dependency listings. Include items mentioned in prose descriptions, changelogs, dependency trees, and configuration files — not only top-level package entries. A package that depends on, provides, vendors, bundles, or embeds a component counts as that component being installed.

2. Review every advisory: For EACH advisory in the supplied list (do not skip any), extract from its 'affected' field the affected product name(s) and version constraint(s). Interpret constraints carefully: 'before X' means < X (X excluded); 'up to and including X' means <= X; '>= A and < B' means A <= v < B; 'through X' means <= X. Multiple affected products or ranges may be listed — the advisory applies if ANY installed product matches ANY of its ranges.

3. Matching rules:
   a. Product-name matching is case-insensitive and tolerant of naming variants, abbreviations, vendor prefixes, spacing, hyphenation, and package suffixes (e.g., 'openssh' matches 'OpenSSH Server'; 'libxml2' matches 'libxml2-dev'; 'linux kernel' matches 'kernel'; 'openssl' matches 'libssl1.1' since the latter provides OpenSSL). When unsure whether a package name refers to the advisory's product, lean toward treating it as a match.
   b. Version checking:
      - Compare versions numerically/semantically, never lexicographically (1.10 > 1.9; 2.0.1 > 2.0; 1.2.10 > 1.2.2).
      - If the installed version string has prefixes ('v', 'r'), epochs, or distro suffixes ('1.2.3-1ubuntu4', '+deb10u1'), compare the upstream version portion against the constraint, ignoring the suffix unless the advisory's range itself references distro-specific versions.
      - 'before X' excludes X itself; 'up to and including X' / 'through X' includes X. Note that a version like '1.2.3-1' is GREATER than '1.2.3', so it is NOT 'before 1.2.3' but IS within '<= 1.2.3' style inclusive 'through' ranges only if the advisory includes such suffixes; when ambiguous, include.
      - If the advisory lists multiple affected ranges for multiple products, apply it if ANY installed product matches ANY range.
      - If the inventory gives no version for a matching product, INCLUDE the advisory (favor recall).
      - If the installed version cannot be definitively shown to be OUTSIDE every stated affected range, INCLUDE the advisory. Version parsing is often ambiguous (missing patch digits, differing formats, pre-release tags, distro backports where the version number is unchanged from an upstream vulnerable release); only exclude on version grounds when you can POSITIVELY establish the installed version is outside every stated affected range for every matching product. Distro-maintained packages often keep the same version while backporting fixes, and conversely may be patched — since you cannot verify patch status, do not exclude on that basis.
   c. Exclusion rules: Exclude an advisory ONLY if (i) the affected product is definitively not present in the inventory (including not being a dependency, submodule, or bundled library of any installed package), or (ii) the installed version is positively established to be outside the affected range per the advisory's own constraints. Never exclude because the description mentions another product, a feature you assume is unused, a component you assume is not loaded, or your outside knowledge of the CVE. Never exclude because the product appears only as a dependency or shared library rather than a primary package.
   d. Never use outside knowledge: only the supplied advisories and the inventory. Never invent CVE IDs or bring in advisories not in the supplied list.

4. Deduplicate: Each applicable advisory ID appears at most once in the answer.

Bias toward inclusion: this task penalizes missed applicable advisories, so when product presence or version applicability is uncertain, INCLUDE the advisory.

Output format: Return ONLY a JSON object of the form {"applicable_cves":["CVE-...",...]} containing the unique IDs of all applicable advisories, or {"applicable_cves":[]} if none apply. No explanations, no markdown, no extra keys.","feedback":{"error_counts":{"invalid_output":0,"missed_applicable":16,"transport_failure":0,"unrelated_product":2,"version_excluded":34},"metrics":{"coverage":1.0,"failure_aware_lower_bound":{"fn":16,"fp":36,"micro_f1":0.6533333333333333,"precision":0.5764705882352941,"recall":0.7538461538461538,"tp":49},"scheduled":24,"valid":24,"valid_answers":{"fn":16,"fp":36,"micro_f1":0.6533333333333333,"precision":0.5764705882352941,"recall":0.7538461538461538,"tp":49}}},"feedback_version":"relational-abstractions-v2","task":"Write an instruction for matching a system inventory to a supplied list of CVE advisories. Input is JSON containing system_profile and advisories. Each advisory supplies its ID, description, and affected information. The answer must be a JSON object whose applicable_cves array contains unique IDs from that supplied list. Return your instruction as a JSON object with one nonempty prompt string of at most 8000 characters.","tier":1}
